svg.title: LabPass AWS infrastructure architecture
svg.desc: Route 53 directs browsers to CloudFront. CloudFront uses a private S3 frontend and HTTPS ALB origin. Two FastAPI EC2 instances span two Availability Zones. A separate EC2 relay polls PostgreSQL outbox records and publishes to SQS. A VPC-connected Lambda worker uses PostgreSQL delivery claims and SES to send email; SQS redrives failed messages to a dead-letter queue. RDS is Single-AZ, isolated and TLS-protected. Private workloads share one NAT gateway and use an S3 gateway endpoint. GitHub Actions uses OIDC roles, ECR, Terraform state and SSM migrations; IAM, Secrets Manager and CloudWatch support the workloads.
svg.text: Workshop booking • transactional outbox • asynchronous email • Terraform and GitHub Actions
PRIVATE APPLICATION SUBNETS / two Availability Zones
Event ID + type · no recipient data
Retries are separate from booking commits
Lambda uses RDS delivery claims before sending.
GitHub Actions → ECR → approved Terraform plan
SSM migration → rolling EC2 / Lambda update → S3 frontend
OIDC roles: publish / plan / apply • reviewer approval • versioned S3 state
Container digests are immutable; CI-scanned images are published without rebuilding.
Logical deployment architecture • baseline: 2 API + 1 relay • Single-AZ RDS • one NAT gateway
